::: {#rem-surprisal-meaning}
#### Unlikely outcomes carry more information

Surprisal is large when an outcome was unlikely,
and it falls to $0$ as the outcome becomes certain.
Correctly predicting heads on one toss of a fair coin is worth $1$ bit;
correctly predicting ten heads in a row is worth $10$ bits.
@mackay2003information [section 2.4] calls $s(x)$ in bits
the *Shannon information content* of the outcome $x$.

:::
